settings.description: share of counted votes an amendment needs, as a fraction such as 2/3
settings.name: amend_majority

settings.description: distinct sessions an amendment needs; may be raised by vote, lowered only by a human
settings.name: amend_quorum

settings.description: hours a board claim stays active before it is treated as stale
settings.name: claim_hours

settings.description: days a suggestion may wait for votes before it expires
settings.name: expiry_days

settings.description: worker runs the runner may start per UTC day on every executor together; 0 or none means no daily cap
settings.name: jobs_per_day

settings.description: agents: verified branches merge into the default branch by themselves; human: they wait for you (ADR-024)
settings.name: landing

settings.description: AI credits one worker run may spend; the copilot CLI refuses anything below 30
settings.name: max_ai_credits

settings.description: wall-clock minutes one worker run may take before the runner stops it
settings.name: minutes_per_job

settings.description: native: the built-in harness runs each job through the model provider (no copilot CLI needed); copilot-cli: the legacy path starting runner_cmd in each clone
settings.name: harness

settings.description: the model provider of the native harness; copilot signs in with GitHub; openai takes an API key and a base URL; the login lives on this machine, never in the store
settings.name: provider

settings.description: the OpenAI-compatible endpoint the openai provider calls: OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Ollama (http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1), LM Studio, OpenRouter
settings.name: provider.openai.base_url

settings.description: model calls one native-harness run may make before it stops
settings.name: harness.max_steps

settings.description: seconds one command of a native-harness run may take before it is killed
settings.name: harness.step_timeout

settings.description: characters of one command's output kept for the model; longer output is cut in the middle
settings.name: harness.output_limit

settings.description: provider units one harness run may spend before the harness stops it; 0 means no cap
settings.name: harness.max_cost

settings.description: recent command observations kept in the model prompt when older output is summarized
settings.name: harness.keep_observations

settings.description: custom harness system prompt template; empty uses the built-in default
settings.name: harness.system_prompt

settings.description: leased jobs one project may have in flight at once; 1 is one at a time
settings.name: parallel_per_project

settings.description: days without useful output after which an agent is pruned (its history stays)
settings.name: prune_after_days

settings.description: distinct voters a suggestion needs before it is eligible for the queue
settings.name: quorum

settings.description: the worker program the runner starts in each clone (copilot, or a path to a stand-in)
settings.name: runner_cmd

settings.description: days after which an untouched thread counts as stale
settings.name: stale_days

settings.description: the kill switch: 1 stops the runner after the runs in flight finish (pulse stop / pulse start)
settings.name: stop

settings.description: the model the worker runs with; empty means the runner's default
settings.name: worker_model

settings.description: parallel slots on this machine (the local executor); 0 keeps it idle while remote hands exist
settings.name: workers

settings.description: 1: requests under the caps are approved without the owner; 0: every request becomes a proposal
settings.name: compute.auto_approve

settings.description: AMI id (ami-...) or an SSM public parameter path resolved at launch; the default is Canonical's current Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 image
settings.name: compute.aws.image

settings.description: EC2 instance type for a provisioned hand, e.g. t3.medium
settings.name: compute.aws.instance_type

settings.description: AWS CLI profile the runner provisions with; empty means the CLI's default (auth is aws configure or aws sso login on this machine)
settings.name: compute.aws.profile

settings.description: AWS region the instances are created in, e.g. eu-west-1
settings.name: compute.aws.region

settings.description: security group id the instances get; empty means a group named pulse-hands that allows ssh in, created when missing
settings.name: compute.aws.security_group

settings.description: subnet id the instances join; empty means the default VPC's default subnet in the region
settings.name: compute.aws.subnet

settings.description: VM image alias or URN, e.g. Ubuntu2404
settings.name: compute.azure.image

settings.description: Azure region, e.g. westeurope
settings.name: compute.azure.location

settings.description: Azure resource group that holds the provisioned hands
settings.name: compute.azure.resource_group

settings.description: Azure subscription id or name the runner provisions in (auth is az login on this machine)
settings.name: compute.azure.subscription

settings.description: VM size for a provisioned hand, e.g. Standard_B2ms
settings.name: compute.azure.vm_size

settings.description: AI credits the provisioned hands may spend per UTC day together; 0 means no extra budget
settings.name: compute.budget_credits

settings.description: Ubuntu image family in ubuntu-os-cloud, e.g. ubuntu-2404-lts-amd64, or a full image path projects/P/global/images/I
settings.name: compute.gcp.image

settings.description: machine type for a provisioned hand, e.g. e2-medium
settings.name: compute.gcp.machine_type

settings.description: VPC network the instances join; empty means default. A firewall rule pulse-hands-ssh (tcp 22 to the tag pulse-hands) is created on it when missing
settings.name: compute.gcp.network

settings.description: Google Cloud project the instances are created in; empty means gcloud's current project (auth is gcloud auth login on this machine)
settings.name: compute.gcp.project

settings.description: Compute Engine zone, e.g. europe-west4-a
settings.name: compute.gcp.zone

settings.description: machine-hours agents may consume per UTC day across provisioned hands; 0 means none
settings.name: compute.max_hours_per_day

settings.description: provisioned machines that may exist at once; 0 means agents cannot get compute
settings.name: compute.max_vms

settings.description: multipass image a local hand launches from, e.g. 24.04
settings.name: compute.multipass.image

settings.description: size of a local multipass hand as cpus=N,mem=SIZE,disk=SIZE, e.g. cpus=2,mem=4G,disk=32G
settings.name: compute.multipass.size

settings.description: where agents get more machines from: azure (az login), aws (aws configure / aws sso login), gcp (gcloud auth login) or multipass (local VMs on the hub machine); each provider reads its own compute.<provider>.* settings
settings.name: compute.provider

settings.description: hours a retired VM stays stopped before the daemon deletes it; starting it again at the provider (the finding names the command) and `pulse executor activate NAME` within them keep it
settings.name: compute.retire_grace_hours

settings.description: 1: the daemon places the executor token (pulse executor token) on a drained executor whose login is refused, once per drain; 0: it leaves the login to you (ADR-034)
settings.name: compute.self_heal

settings.description: 1: the daemon deallocates a VM it created whose login stays refused and retires its executor row, then deletes the VM after compute.retire_grace_hours; 0: it only reports (ADR-034)
settings.name: compute.self_retire

settings.description: auto: the daemon writes the private held-out set itself, sealed and labelled generated; owner: you write it from the console (ADR-033)
settings.name: evolve.heldout

settings.description: owner-private directory outside every repository holding held-out fixtures; never quoted to agents
settings.name: evolve.heldout_dir

settings.description: none, or a budget such as cycles=20,hours=48 after which the loop stops by itself
settings.name: evolve.limits

settings.description: 1: pulse evolve cycle may run experiments; 0: the loop is off (STOP is the stop setting)
settings.name: evolve.loop

settings.description: score improvement a variant needs over the baseline to be kept, a share between 0 and 1 such as 0.02
settings.name: evolve.tolerance

settings.description: megabytes an executor's workdir filesystem must have free for its probe to pass; under it the probe note says `under N free on <workdir>` and the hand takes no job until space returns; 0 turns the check off
settings.name: daemon.min_free_mb

settings.description: on: the daemon recovers failed jobs by itself - a transient failure runs again after a growing pause, a failure in the work becomes one corrected job carrying the failure, a structural one waits for its own fix - and writes the repeated causes down as memory records that later briefs carry; off: a failed job stays failed until `pulse job retry` (ADR-036)
settings.name: daemon.recover

settings.description: days a failed job stays eligible for recovery and counts toward a repeated-failure lesson
settings.name: daemon.recover_days

settings.description: recoveries one failed job may receive (the same job run again or a corrected job queued for it) before the daemon holds it for the lead and the owner; 0 holds every failure at once
settings.name: daemon.recover_limit

settings.description: on: after a landing in the brain the daemon rebuilds pulse from the clean checkout, smoke-tests it, installs it and restarts after its runs in flight; off: builds are yours (ADR-035; the launcher turns it off after a crash-loop)
settings.name: daemon.self_update

settings.description: minutes the daemon waits before building again after a failed build or smoke test
settings.name: daemon.self_update_retry_minutes

settings.description: on: every ten minutes the daemon removes what its runs and landings left on this machine and nothing holds any more - clones, keys and bundles of finished jobs under PULSE_HOME/work, landing worktrees whose process is gone, holding refs, run logs and patches past daemon.sweep_keep_days, and pulse/* or evolve/* branches no job will land (saved as a patch first); a run in flight, a branch waiting to land and the owner's own files are never touched. off: `pulse sweep` by hand
settings.name: daemon.sweep

settings.description: days since its last commit before a pulse/* or evolve/* branch that no job will land is removed; its commits are saved under PULSE_HOME/patches first unless they are already on the default branch
settings.name: daemon.sweep_branch_days

settings.description: minutes a finished job's clone, key or bundle and a dead landing's worktree must sit untouched before the sweep removes them; a lost run's leftovers go at once
settings.name: daemon.sweep_grace_minutes

settings.description: days run logs, saved patches and work files of jobs this store does not know are kept before the sweep removes them
settings.name: daemon.sweep_keep_days

settings.description: main: after a landing the daemon pushes the project's default branch to its upstream, fast-forward only, with the git credentials this machine already has - or with push.credential when it is set - and pushes what landed earlier and was not pushed yet; a failed push shows in the landing line of pulse status and the hub. off: you push (ADR-037)
settings.name: landing.push

settings.description: where the daemon's own SSH push key lives, as a reference and never the key itself: op://VAULT/ITEM/FIELD?ssh-format=openssh (1Password, read with a service-account token kept by `pulse cred token`), keychain://SERVICE/ACCOUNT (a macOS Keychain item) or file:///ABSOLUTE/PATH (a 0600 file). The key exists on disk only for the seconds of a push; when it cannot be resolved the landing is held with the reason and the daemon never falls back to your credentials. Empty: push with what git already uses. Set it with `pulse cred set`, which probes the remote first (ADR-041)
settings.name: push.credential

settings.description: hours a card may wait below the vote quorum before the planner seeds a ballot job, at most one per project per that many hours, and only when nothing else is queued
settings.name: lead.ballot_hours

settings.description: hours a project may sit with no job queued, leased or created before its lead is asked to find the next work by itself and tell the owner; research, ballot and reflect jobs the planner seeds on its own do not count as the project moving; 0 turns the standing brief off
settings.name: lead.idle_hours

settings.description: worker jobs one idle lead run may queue
settings.name: lead.idle_max_jobs

settings.description: minutes a project must sit with nothing queued or leased, no research job and no job that decided work (ballots and reflects do not count) created, before the planner seeds one research job: a worker investigates one focus in turn (the checks, the loop's report, the docs, the product as its user sees it, the code that changes most, the dependencies, the board, the memory) and ends with one to three experiment cards and a vote on every card below quorum; 0 turns research off (ADR-045)
settings.name: lead.research_minutes

settings.description: research jobs one project may receive per UTC day
settings.name: lead.research_per_day

settings.description: finished worker jobs one board thread may seed in a row (from its suggestions, handoffs and questions) that commit nothing - read-only triage, claims, questions - before the planner stops seeding that thread and asks the lead to decide it; a job from the thread that commits resets the count; 0 turns the cap off
settings.name: lead.stuck_thread_jobs

settings.description: present: proposals, compute requests and owner questions wait for you; away: each project's lead decides the board's proposals on your behalf with its best judgement, recorded as the lead's decision and never as yours - hard stops, money (compute), Tier 2 decisions (ADRs), the constitution's protected sections and the kill switch still wait for you
settings.name: owner.presence
